General scientific education will be available to everyone, focusing on the scientific method, correct thinking habits, and the ability to generalize from facts while making deductions. However, only a few will have encyclopedic minds or advanced sociological knowledge. It would be tragic for mankind if theoretical speculation became the sole guide for society, with science in full control of social administration. Such domination would lead to the brutalization of humanity.

Simon Freud practiced medicine in Vienna and was a psychologist, seeing many young women as patients. When they would say, "I'm hysterical," it meant they were depressed or anxious, unable to control their emotions. If a man talked to them, they might stutter, run away, have difficulty with personal relationships, and experience sleep issues and sweating. Freud asked his patients why these issues arose, and when they mentioned being raped by their fathers as children, Freud found this strange but recognized the pattern in many cases.

Freud collected research on this issue and published a paper titled "The Psychology of Women's Hysteria," confirming that trauma, especially sexual trauma, was common among children from respected families. He noted that parents or trusted individuals often sexually abused children, and the idea that these accounts were just fantasies weakened with the frequency of such confessions.

To understand hysteria symptoms, one must start with Joseph Brewer's discovery: the experiences causing trauma are reproduced in patients' psychical life through symbolic mimicry. This means the women experiencing hysterical symptoms had indeed suffered real traumas during their youth and were not merely imagining them.
